---
title: "🎨 Customise charts and maps"
description: >
  fao_settings(): language, theme, colour palettes, map projection and centre, fonts, grid
  lines, resolution, PowerPoint output and data folders.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
FAO27 <- suppressMessages(fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast", plot = FALSE))
```

```{r data-source, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
data_source()
```

```{r page-language, include = FALSE}
page_lang <- getOption("faofishingreport.lang", "en")
```

All charts and maps follow a few settings, set once per R session with `fao_settings()`. Run it
without arguments to see the current settings:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_settings()
#>   lang            en
#>   theme           bw
#>   base_size       12
#>   palette         npg
#>   map_palette     deep-orange
#>   map_center      0
#>   map_projection  longlat
#>   map_land        grey90
#>   map_ocean       NA
#>   grid            FALSE
#>   dpi             600
#>   pptx            FALSE
#>   data_dir        C:/Users/<you>/AppData/Roaming/R/data/R/faofishingreport
#>   online          TRUE
#>   sst             ersst5
#>   silent          FALSE
#>   font            SimSun
```

`fao_settings(...)` takes the settings as `name = value`, and one more argument, `reset`:

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `...` | Settings to change, as `name = value` (table below) | |
| `reset` | `TRUE` first restores all settings to their defaults | `FALSE` |

The settings:

| Setting | Choices | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `lang` | Language of charts: `"en"`, `"zh"`, `"both"`; the `lang` argument of a function takes precedence | `"en"` |
| `theme` | `"bw"`, `"classic"`, `"minimal"`, `"light"`, `"linedraw"`, `"gray"`, `"dark"`, or a ggplot2 theme object; maps and pie charts keep a minimal theme | `"bw"` |
| `base_size` | Base font size of the theme | `12` |
| `font` | Font family of chart text (see [Fonts](#fonts)) | chosen for the system |
| `palette` | Colours of categories (countries, species, groups): a ggsci palette (`"npg"`, `"lancet"`, ...), an RColorBrewer palette (`"Set1"`, ...), a base R palette (`grDevices::palette.pals()`, e.g. `"Okabe-Ito"`; `grDevices::hcl.pals()`, e.g. `"viridis"`), or a vector of colours | `"npg"` |
| `map_palette` | Colours of map values: a Material Design palette of ggsci (`"deep-orange"`, `"blue"`, `"teal"`, ...), an RColorBrewer palette (`"YlOrRd"`, `"Blues"`, ...), a viridis option (`"viridis"`, `"magma"`, `"plasma"`, `"inferno"`, `"cividis"`, `"mako"`, `"rocket"`, `"turbo"`), a `grDevices::hcl.pals()` name, or a vector of colours | `"deep-orange"` |
| `map_center` | Central longitude of maps: `0` (longitudes -180 to 180, Atlantic in the centre) or `180` (0 to 360, Pacific in the centre); `"-180-180"` and `"0-360"` are also accepted | `0` |
| `map_projection` | `"longlat"`, `"robinson"`, `"mollweide"`, `"equal_earth"`, `"winkel_tripel"`, `"mercator"`, or a PROJ string or EPSG code (then `map_center` is not applied) | `"longlat"` |
| `map_land` | Colour of countries without data on maps | `"grey90"` |
| `map_ocean` | Colour of the ocean on maps | `NA` (no fill) |
| `grid` | Background grid lines (graticules on maps) | `FALSE` |
| `dpi` | Resolution of the PNG files | `600` |
| `pptx` | Also save editable PowerPoint files (uses the eoffice package) | `FALSE` |
| `data_dir` | Folder of downloaded FAO data (see [💾 FAO data](data.html)) | `NULL`: the user data folder of R, see `fao_data_dir()` |
| `online` | Whether functions may connect to the internet to look for the newest FishBase release; `FALSE` works offline with the downloaded copy (see [🐠 FishBase](fishbase.html)) | `TRUE` |
| `sst` | Sea surface temperature data of `fao_area_sst()` and `mean_temperature_catch()`: `"ersst5"` (built in), a product downloaded with `download_sst_data()` (e.g. `"hadisst1"`), or the path of your own NetCDF file or folder (see [🌡️ Sea temperature](sst-mtc.html)) | `"ersst5"` |
| `silent` | Whether the CMSY++ functions work without progress bars and messages; their `silent` argument takes precedence (see [📉 CMSY++](cmsy.html)) | `FALSE` |

`fao_settings(reset = TRUE)` restores the defaults. A wrong name or value gives an error at once,
with the choices available. Each setting is stored as the R option `faofishingreport.<name>`, so
it can also be set with `options()`, e.g. in an `.Rprofile` file. `fao_settings()` returns the
current settings invisibly, as a list.

## 🌐 Language

Every analysis has a `lang` argument; `fao_settings(lang = ...)` changes the default for all of them.
`"both"` writes Chinese and English together, e.g. "百万吨 (Million Tonnes)" and "挪威 Norway".

```{r, figures = "area_country.png"}
fao_settings(lang = "zh")
fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 6))
```

```{r, figures = "area_country.png"}
fao_settings(lang = "both")
fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 6))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
fao_settings(lang = page_lang)
```

Go back to English with `fao_settings(lang = "en")`. The older argument `ZH = TRUE` still works
and means `lang = "zh"`.

## 🖼️ Themes

```{r, figures = "area_country.png"}
fao_settings(theme = "classic")
fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 6))
```

```{r, figures = "area_country.png"}
fao_settings(theme = "minimal", base_size = 14)
fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 6))
```

Any ggplot2 theme can be used, e.g. `fao_settings(theme = ggplot2::theme_light(base_size = 13))`.

## 🎨 Colour palettes

`palette` colours countries, species and groups:

```{r, figures = "area_country.png"}
fao_settings(theme = "bw", base_size = 12, palette = "lancet")
fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 6))
```

```{r, figures = "area_country.png"}
fao_settings(palette = "Okabe-Ito")        # suitable for colour-blind readers
fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 6))
```

```{r, figures = "area_country.png"}
fao_settings(palette = c("#0B2E5B", "#16A6B6", "#F28E2B", "#E15759", "#59A14F", "#B07AA1"))
fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 6))
fao_settings(palette = "npg")
```

Palettes of the ggsci package include `"npg"`, `"aaas"`, `"nejm"`, `"lancet"`, `"jama"`, `"jco"`,
`"d3"`; of RColorBrewer `"Set1"`, `"Set2"`, `"Dark2"`, `"Paired"`; of base R
`grDevices::palette.pals()` (e.g. the Okabe-Ito palette for colour-blind readers, Okabe and Ito
2008) and `grDevices::hcl.pals()` (Zeileis et al. 2020). More categories than a palette has are
interpolated.

## 🗺️ Map projections

The same map, the catch of each country in area 27, in each projection:

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_projection = "longlat")      # plain longitude-latitude (default)
fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_projection = "robinson")
fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_projection = "equal_earth")
fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_projection = "mollweide")
fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_projection = "winkel_tripel")
fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_projection = "mercator")
fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

The named projections and the PROJ projection each one uses (the maps are drawn with sf, which
uses the PROJ library):

| `map_projection` | Projection | PROJ | Properties |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"longlat"` | Plain longitude-latitude (equidistant cylindrical, plate carrée) | `EPSG:4326`; `+proj=eqc` with `map_center = 180` | Simple; areas far from the equator are enlarged |
| `"robinson"` | Robinson (Robinson 1974) | `+proj=robin` | Compromise world map: neither equal-area nor conformal |
| `"equal_earth"` | Equal Earth (Šavrič et al. 2019) | `+proj=eqearth` | Equal-area, with straight parallels |
| `"mollweide"` | Mollweide (Snyder 1987) | `+proj=moll` | Equal-area, elliptical outline |
| `"winkel_tripel"` | Winkel tripel | `+proj=wintri` | Compromise world map with low overall distortion |
| `"mercator"` | Mercator (Snyder 1987) | `+proj=merc` | Conformal; areas grow strongly towards the poles, cut at 80° S and 84° N |

Any other projection can be given as a PROJ string or EPSG code, e.g.
`fao_settings(map_projection = "+proj=natearth")` or `"EPSG:3857"`.

## 🌏 Pacific-centred maps

`map_center = 180` shows longitudes 0 to 360, with the Pacific in the centre. Areas and countries
that the data split at the dateline (e.g. the Pacific areas, Russia) are joined again:

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_projection = "robinson", map_center = 180)
fishing_area_data("Pacific, Northwest")
```

Fishing area maps show the land without country borders, and the analysed country in red:

```{r, figures = "fishing_area_map"}
country_analysis("Norway")
```

Countries are drawn from the Natural Earth map units (1:50m), matched to the FAO countries on
their ISO 3 codes; the fishing areas from the FAO layer of the major fishing areas, simplified for
world maps.

## 🖌️ Map colours

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_projection = "robinson", map_center = 0, map_palette = "viridis")
fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

```{r, figures = "area_country_map"}
fao_settings(map_palette = "YlOrRd", map_land = "grey85", map_ocean = "#EAF4FB")
fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast")
```

The `fill_scale` argument of `fishing_area_data()`, `species_country()` and
`country_analysis()` overrides `map_palette` for one call.

```{r, include = FALSE}
fao_settings(reset = TRUE)
fao_settings(dpi = 100, lang = page_lang)
```

## 🔤 Fonts {#fonts}

The font is chosen for the operating system so that Chinese text displays: SimSun on Windows,
Songti SC on macOS, Noto Serif CJK SC on Linux, or the next installed Chinese font (and `"sans"`
if none is found). Change it with:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_font()                            # the current font
fao_settings(font = "Microsoft YaHei")
```

`fao_font()` has one argument:

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `family` | Font family to use from now on, e.g. `"Microsoft YaHei"`; `NULL` only returns the current font | `NULL` |

It returns the font family name. `fao_settings(font = ...)`, `fao_font(...)` and
`options(faofishingreport.font = ...)` do the same. The fonts tried on each system:

| System | Fonts, in order |
|---|---|
| Windows | SimSun, NSimSun, Microsoft YaHei, SimHei, DengXian, KaiTi |
| macOS | Songti SC, STSong, PingFang SC, Heiti SC, Hiragino Sans GB, Arial Unicode MS |
| Linux | Noto Serif CJK SC, Noto Sans CJK SC, Source Han Serif SC, Source Han Sans SC, WenQuanYi Zen Hei, WenQuanYi Micro Hei, AR PL UMing CN |

The installed fonts are listed with the systemfonts package. PNG files are drawn with the ragg
package, which finds any installed font by name; PowerPoint files use the same font name.

## 📐 Grid lines, resolution and PowerPoint

```{r, figures = "area_country.png"}
fao_settings(grid = TRUE)
fishing_area_country(FAO27$area_data, rank_range = c(1, 6))
fao_settings(grid = FALSE)
```

PowerPoint files are written with the eoffice package, installed with faofishingreport; on macOS
it also needs [XQuartz](https://www.xquartz.org).

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_settings(dpi = 300)      # smaller PNG files
fao_settings(pptx = TRUE)    # also editable PowerPoint in figures/pptx/
fishing_area_species(FAO27$area_data, pptx = TRUE)   # or for one call only
```

## ⚙️ Arguments of each function

Besides the settings, the analysis functions have their own arguments; `lang`, `pptx` and
`fill_scale` override the settings for one call. Each article has a table of all of them:

| Functions | All arguments |
|---|---|
| `fishing_area_data()`, `fishing_area_species()`, `fishing_area_country()` (line widths, point sizes, text sizes and colours) | [🌊 Fishing area analysis](fishing-areas.html) |
| `species_country()`, `country_species()`, `country_analysis()` | [🐟 Species and countries](species-countries.html) |
| `check_fao_update()`, `download_fao_data()`, `load_fao_data()`, `fao_data_info()`, `fao_translate()` | [💾 FAO data](data.html) |
| Summary analyses, e.g. `stock_status()`, `peak_trend()` | [📈 Composition, stock status and trends](status-trends.html), [🔍 Data quality, diversity and fleets](quality-diversity-fleets.html) |
| `fao_report()` | [📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and PDF](report.html) |

## 📝 Translations

Chinese names of countries, species and areas come from FAO. The Chinese names of ISSCAAP groups,
major groups and income groups (`inst/extdata/group_names_zh.csv`) and all chart labels
(`inst/extdata/chart_labels.csv`) are plain CSV files: edit them in the package source and
reinstall the package to change the wording.
